verdict.rationale: Pipecat documents STT latency tuning: it ships measured P99 latency values per supported STT service so turn detection can account for that delay, and it defines a Time To Final Segment metric. Built-in metrics also back its 'ultra-low latency' positioning, but the evidence covers only the speech-to-text slice of the pipeline, not end-to-end voice latency. missing for 10: documented end-to-end voice-to-voice latency numbers, tuning guidance across LLM/TTS/transport stages, published benchmarks that directly substantiate the 'ultra-low latency' claim, independent corroboration of measured latency.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can see documented end-to-end voice latency numbers or tuning guidance backing the platform's speed claims

citations.quote: Pipecat ships with measured P99 latency values for each supported service so that turn detection can account for this delay automatically.
Time To Final Segment (TTFS) measures how long it takes from the moment a user stops speaking until the STT service delivers the final transcript.
Pipecat offers built-in metrics for both, which can be enabled with straightforward configuration options.
